title: Niryasa 2. The Description of the Sub-branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu
html:
Srinivasa's sub-branches: the disciples of Ramachandra Kaviraja; the daughters-in-law and disciples of Ishvari; the disciples of Hemalata — among them the author himself, Yadunandana of Malihati; the disciples of Gati-Govinda

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda!
Glory to Advaita-chandra, glory to Gaura's devotees!

2Now I shall tell — listen — of Prabhu's sub-branches;
I shall count only some of the chief ones.

3The branches of Ramachandra Kaviraja Thakura —
I shall tell only a little of them, to point the way.

4Sri Vallabha Majumdar, born in a brahmana family —
the Kaviraja, overcome by mercy, showed him mercy.

5All his time passes in talk of Krishna;
in the waves of prema he loses himself in bliss.

6Another of his servants is Harirama Acharya,
a great pandita, noble in all virtues.

7His son is Gopikanta Chakravarti,
devoted to Hari-nama, renowned for his prema.

8He is his father's servant (disciple), a king of devotees;
to list all his disciples would take too long.

9A disciple of the Kaviraja is Balarama Kavipati,
whose expressions of prema are extraordinary.

10The Kaviraja's disciples and grand-disciples filled the world;
all of them were bhagavatas and showed mercy to living beings.

11I cannot name all the Kaviraja's disciples;
for my own purification I sing their glories.

12Jayakrishna Acharya, Jagadisha Acharya
and Shyamavallabha Acharya — these three are most noble.

13Further disciples of Ishvari,1 most virtuous,
are the two daughters-in-law, virtuous, abodes of good qualities.

14Both love each other dearly, full of the expressions of prema,
with hearts compassionate to deliver all living beings.

15Both always, without pause, take Hari-nama:
day and night they chant the name, counting, without rest.

16Until they have taken a hundred thousand names they will not drink even water;
their eyes are always full of tears, their hearts of bliss.

17Hear with one mind the names of the two daughters-in-law —
names by hearing which one's desires are fulfilled.

18The elder daughter-in-law is named Satyabhama Thakurani,
the other Chandramukhi, a jewel of virtues.

19Together they always speak of bhajana;
their bodies are full of prema, their limbs glowing with joy.

20What they heard from the lips of their Ishvari,
that, immersed in happiness, they recite — the hymns

21that Sri Rupa Gosani and Sri Dasa Gosani,
the two Prabhus, uttered in joy:

22the Ashtaka of Mahaprabhu and the Chaitanya-kalpavriksha
they recite with joy, finding great happiness;

23the Karpanya-panjika and the Hari-kusumanjali,
the Vilapa-kusumanjali they read with eagerness;

24the Chatu-pushpanjali called Premambhoja-maranda,
the Manah-shiksha and the rest — all these they read.2

25Every moment both say "Sri Radha-Govinda";
in supreme bliss both always perform bhajana freely.

26Their disciples and grand-disciples filled the world;
I could not write down their names.

27Radhavallabha Chakravarti, and Vrindavana
Chakravarti, a worthy man, foremost among devotees.

28Vrindavani Thakurani is his disciple;
and also Radhavinoda Chakravarti and Kishori Chakravarti —

29both disciples of their mother, followers of Ishvari.
All of them have very many disciples.

30Now I shall tell of the Thakura's daughter, Srila Hemalata,
renowned for the many disciples of Srimati.3

31Sri Subalachandra Thakura, ever full of bliss —
his nephew is his disciple, a worthy man.

32Sri Gokula Chakravarti is her servant,
a great giver, full of prema, profound in conduct.

33Another disciple of hers is Radhavallabha Thakura,
a resident of Mandalagrama, a hero among devotees.

34Sri Vallabha Dasa is another servant of hers,
a resident of Gomai, the very essence of anuraga.

35Another is the lowly Yadunandana, a Vaidya servant by name,4
living in the village of Malihati — worthless, devoid of prema.

36Falling at her feet, he begs for mercy,
thinking in his heart, "Perhaps some day she will be merciful."

37This semblance of a servant has never served,
yet by her goodness he has caught hold of those feet.

38Kanurama Chakravarti is her servant;
Darpanarayana and Chandisimha are two servants of hers;

39Ramacharana, Madhu Bishvas, the Vaidya Radhakanta —
how many more shall I name? I know no more.

40Jagadisha Kaviraja is another disciple of hers;
Radhavallabha, the Kaviraja's brother, is the best of devotees.

41The disciples of Sri Gati Prabhu5 are first of all his sons:
Sri Krishnaprasada Thakura, profound of heart,

42Sri Sundarananda and Sri Hari Thakura —
three sons and disciples, three heroes among devotees.

43Of his three wives the youngest
became a vessel of Prabhu's mercy;

44the eldest of all is named Sri Satyabhama:
she showed mercy to Sri Radha-Madhava.6

45Jagadananda Thakura is a servant of Gati Prabhu,
most sweet in disposition, endowed with many virtues.

46To Tulasirama Dasa's son Sri Ghanashyama
he showed mercy, filled with compassion.

47Sri Kandarpa Raya Chatta is a servant of Gati Prabhu:
his fame and virtues are known in the world.

48The daughter of Sri Vyasa is named Sri Kanakapriya:
to her he mercifully showed mercy.

49The son of Janaki Bishvas is Sri Hadagovinda:
both (father and son) serve Prabhu's feet with body and mind.

50The son of Prasada Bishvas is Vrindavana Dasa:
his fidelity and love for Prabhu's feet, his faith, are supreme.

51Vrajamohana Chattaraja is another disciple of his,
and Sri Purushottama Chakravarti another disciple of his.

52Another disciple of Prabhu is named Jayaramadasa,
sweet in character, who lives in the village of Sonarundi.

53Another servant is Radhakrishna Acharya Thakura,
who reached the summit of bhajana, rich in virtues.

54Krishnaprasada Chakravarti is a disciple of Gati Prabhu:
he ever remains in the rasa of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

55His nephew is Sri Madana Chakravarti,
always longing for the rasa of the nectar of Krishna's pastimes.

56Vallavikanta Chakravarti is one of his disciples,
ever absorbed in madhurya-rasa.

57Ghanashyama Kaviraja is a vessel of his mercy.
To point the way I have shown only a little.

58Countless are the servants of Gati Prabhu, king of devotees:
I do not know their names, and to write them down would take too long.

59Prabhu's sub-branches cannot be written down;
I have shown only a little, to point the way.

60I am most dull-witted and do not know their greatness;
do not count it an offence, be merciful.

61Do not count it a fault if I have written the names out of order;
I bow to the feet of all — be pleased.

62This narrative of the Karnananda is an extract of nectar:
at its touch on the ear, the joy of prema is born in the devotees.

63The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

64Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the rasa of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the second niryasa of the Sri Karnananda, called "The Description of the Sub-branches of Sri Acharya Prabhu".

Notes

  1. Ishvari Thakurani, Srinivasa's elder wife. Her "two daughters-in-law" are the wives of her sons.
  2. Hymns of Rupa Gosvami and Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami from the Stavavali and Stavamala: the Sri Chaitanyashtaka, the Chaitanya-kalpavriksha (probably Raghunatha Dasa's Gauranga-stava-kalpataru), the Karpanya-panjika, the Vilapa-kusumanjali, the Premambhoja-maranda, the Chatu-pushpanjali, the Manah-shiksha and others. The Hari-kusumanjali is an unclear title (perhaps the Sri Radha-kusumanjali or another hymn).
  3. Thakurjhi: "the Thakura's daughter" (Srinivasa's); Srimati is the same Hemalata (cf. 1.268).
  4. Here the author names himself: Yadunandana, a Vaidya by birth, of the village of Malihati, disciple of Hemalata Thakurani.
  5. Gati Prabhu is Gati-Govinda, Srinivasa's youngest son.
  6. The sense is probably that she initiated a certain Sri Radha-Madhava (a disciple); it might also mean "served the Deity of Radha-Madhava".
